reference_items.stem:
Jay has to draw a shape.
- It must have 5 sides.
- It must have one line of symmetry.
Jay has started to draw the shape.
Complete Jay’s shape.

Correct shape drawn which has 5 sides and 1 line of symmetry. The new vertex must be within ±2 mm of the line of symmetry (accept the new vertex anywhere on the line of symmetry, provided there are 5 sides).

reference_items.stem: Which rectangle is NOT divided into 4 equal parts?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided into 4 equal smaller rectangles]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided into 4 equal horizontal strips]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided by three parallel diagonal lines]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectangular figures labeled A, B, C, and D, each partitioned into 4 regions:
- Option A: Divided into 4 equal quadrants by a vertical line and a horizontal line through the center.
- Option B: Divided into two squares by a central vertical line, with each square bisected by a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 4 identical right-angled triangles.
- Option C: Divided into 4 equal horizontal bands by three evenly spaced horizontal lines.
- Option D: Divided into 4 unequal regions by three parallel diagonal lines sloping up and to the right, creating two corner triangles and two trapezoids of unequal sizes.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

A.

USE: 1 Triangle Tile and
1 Trapezoid Tile
MAKE: A 4-sided figure
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors:
Correct 4-sided figure turned in any position
[Image: A parallelogram composed of one trapezoid tile and one triangle tile]
Makes a larger triangle
Makes a 4-sided figure, but not using the specified tiles, e.g., a larger parallelogram.
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part A response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: In which of the following figures is the dotted line a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a square into two opposite trapezoids.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a rectangle into two opposite right angle triangles.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a pentagon into a trapezoid and an irregular pentagon.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a hexagon in the middle.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes, each intersected by a dotted line:
- Option A shows a square with a tilted dotted line that enters through the top side near the top-left corner and exits through the bottom side near the bottom-right corner, dividing the square into two non-congruent trapezoids.
- Option B shows a horizontal rectangle with a dotted line running along the diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner.
- Option C shows a regular pentagon with one vertex at the top and a horizontal base at the bottom. A slightly slanted, nearly horizontal dotted line cuts through the left and right sides below the center, dividing it into an upper portion and a lower trapezoid.
- Option D shows a regular hexagon with horizontal top and bottom edges. A vertical dotted line passes through the exact center, bisecting the top and bottom edges into two identical mirror-image halves.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
